risk_if_not_implemented: Without Risk Management Resourcing, risks may remain unidentified, unowned or unmanaged, leaving decision-makers without a defensible basis for prioritization and treatment. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Uncontrolled Internal Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-4), Loss of Critical Knowledge / Capability (R-PE-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Economic Shock / Market Disruption (MT-16), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Risk Management Resourcing (RSK-03) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Risk Management Program
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls that are aligned with:
(1) The organization's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM); and
(2) Industry-recognized cybersecurity risk management practices.
compensating_control_2.justification: Risk Management Program (RSK-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Risk Management Resourcing (RSK-03) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
